title: Implement prefill governor and eviction-latency smoothing for GPU capacity events
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Multiple hosted API capacity incidents in Q1 showed that aggressive prefill/prefetch and synchronous eviction logic can trigger queue amplification and rapid GPU pool exhaustion. Symptoms observed: sudden queue length spikes, long tail request latency, simultaneous prefetch bursts from multiple tenants, and eviction storms that cause transient latency regressions across lanes.

Problem statement: We currently allow uncontrolled prefill concurrency and run eviction/slot-reclaim as immediate, parallel work. Under bursty traffic this produces: (1) prefills that saturate slot allocation before autoscaler reacts, (2) eviction churn that increases scheduling latency and queue growth, and (3) poor telemetry to attribute root cause to prefill vs. external load.

Proposal: Ship a two-part mitigation: a) Prefill Governor - rate-shearing controller that caps concurrent prefill operations per-tenant and per-pool, with exponential backoff and jitter when queue pressure crosses thresholds. b) Eviction Latency Smoothing - a staggered eviction executor that enforces a controllable max concurrency, exponentially weighted spacing between evictions, and a graceful fallback to soft-degrade policy if latency budgets are threatened.

Design highlights:
- Prefill Governor parameters: tenant_prefill_limit, pool_prefill_burst, pressure_thresholds (soft/hard), backoff_multiplier, jitter_seed. Default values conservative to minimize customer-visible regressions.
- Eviction Smoothing: eviction_batch_size, inter_eviction_delay_ms, long-tail-cap (max continuous evictions per minute). Supports immediate bypass only for critical security-driven evictions.
- Telemetry: add gauge/series metrics (gpu.pool.current_prefills, gpu.pool.prefill_failures, gpu.pool.eviction_in_flight, gpu.pool.eviction_rate_smoothed) and distributed tracing spans for prefill/eviction windows to attribute impact to tenants.
- Safety/rollback: feature gated behind runtime flag and per-pool config. Ramp will start in staging, then canary to 5% of pools, 25%, 100%. Immediate rollback will disable governor and restore previous eviction concurrency settings.

Trade-offs considered:
- Increased request tail latency for some cold-start flows vs reduced burst-driven pool exhaustion. We opt to prioritize platform stability and predictable degradation over lower 99.99 latency for cold-prefill paths.
- Prefill limits could hurt large batch customers; mitigation: soft burst allowance and an override path for dedicated tenants via contract.

Success metrics:
- 75% reduction in pool-wide queue-length spikes during incoming surge tests compared to baseline.
- <10% increase in median cold-start latency in controlled load tests.
- No increase in error-rate (5xx) attributable to governor after canary.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement feature flags + config knobs (ENG branch) and unit tests.
2) Staging integration + chaos test with synthetic surge (kubernetes pod-surge + tenant-preheat scripts).
3) Canary 5% pools for 48 hours with tight telemetry checks.
4) Extend to 25% then full rollout if metrics stable.

Telemetry dashboards and alerts (initial):
- Dashboard: /dashboards/gpu/prefill-governor (placeholder) shows queue length, in-flight prefill, eviction_in_flight, eviction_rate_smoothed.
- Pager rule: if gpu.pool.queue_length > 80th-percentile-by-pool for 5 min AND eviction_in_flight > 5 => P1 alert.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for rate-limiter behavior and jitter/backoff correctness.
- Integration test simulating 100 tenants with bursty traffic and verifying queue growth cap.
- Load test that compares eviction storm scenario pre/post change.
